TenderRegistry.note: Subname registry for tender.eth, deployed via VerifiableFactory. Owner (deployer) holds TENDER_REGISTRY_OWNER_ROLES.

TenderResolver.note: One resolver instance serves tender.eth and every subname beneath it (roles are granted at ROOT_RESOURCE, which is resolver-instance-wide). NOT PublicResolverV2 -- see ens.ts for why.

incident.summary: First setup attempt deployed real, working contracts but pointed every subsequent write at the wrong addresses.
incident.cause: VerifiableFactory.ProxyDeployed's `sender` and `proxyAddress` params are indexed (confirmed against on-chain topics). The first script version assumed all four event params were non-indexed and manually sliced `data` by byte offset to extract `proxyAddress`. That slice actually read the `salt` field's tail 20 bytes -- a pseudorandom hash tail that happened to look exactly like a plausible address.
incident.effect: setSubregistry, register("alice"), and setText were sent to that address. All returned status:success (a call to an address with no bytecode is a no-op that never reverts), so nothing on the surface indicated failure -- only a direct getCode/getOwner read against the target exposed it.
incident.fix: Replaced manual event-data slicing with viem's decodeEventLog against a corrected ABI (indexed: true on sender/proxyAddress). Every write in the corrected script is now followed by an independent read that must match before the script continues -- a receipt's status:success is treated as necessary, not sufficient.
incident.resolution: Re-ran end to end. TenderRegistry and TenderResolver above are confirmed via getCode (non-empty) and via getOwner/text reads that match exactly what was written.
